description: Verify that DUT accepts an IPv4 UDP packet whose Destination Address is the Limited Broadcast (255.255.255.255) — must be received like a unicast for upper-layer protocols (RFC 791 §3.2, RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3)
approach:
[Objective]
Limited broadcast (255.255.255.255) is a one-shot announcement to every host on the local segment. Hosts must receive packets to this address and dispatch them to the appropriate protocol stack just like unicast — for UDP this means the application bound to the destination port sees the datagram.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 UDP packet
   • dst_ip = 255.255.255.255   ← key trigger
   • dst_port = a port DUT's upper-tester listens on

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester acknowledges receipt of the UDP datagram (via test-side query interface)

[Pass condition]
DUT received and delivered the UDP datagram to its upper-tester.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT received but mis-delivered (e.g. dropped to wrong handler)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not receive the datagram within the window — broadcast filter too strict

verdicts.Pass: DUT delivered the limited-broadcast UDP to upper-tester — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received but mis-delivered the UDP datagram
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not receive the datagram — broadcast accepted-list too strict
